title: 1972 AHSME Problem 1
statement: The lengths in inches of the three sides of each of four triangles \(\mathrm{I},\) \(\mathrm{II},\) \(\mathrm{III},\) and \(\mathrm{IV}\) are as follows: \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}\quad&3,4,5\\ \mathrm{II}\quad&4,7\frac12,8\frac12\\ \mathrm{III}\quad&7,24,25\\ \mathrm{IV}\quad&3\frac12,4\frac12,5\frac12 \end{aligned} \] Of these four given triangles, the only right triangles are:

solutions.text:
For triangles \(\mathrm{I},\) \(\mathrm{II},\) and \(\mathrm{III},\) the relevant equalities are \[ \begin{aligned} 3^2+4^2&=5^2,\\ 4^2+\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^2 &=\left(\frac{17}{2}\right)^2,\\ 7^2+24^2&=25^2. \end{aligned} \] For \(\mathrm{IV},\) \[ \begin{aligned} \left(\frac72\right)^2+\left(\frac92\right)^2 &=\frac{130}{4},\\ \left(\frac{11}{2}\right)^2&=\frac{121}{4}. \end{aligned} \] These values are unequal. Thus precisely \(\mathrm{I},\) \(\mathrm{II},\) and \(\mathrm{III}\) are right triangles.

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Compare the square of each longest side with the sum of the squares of the other two sides
Clear the halves in triangles \(\mathrm{II}\) and \(\mathrm{IV}\) before comparing
